foot.about: The lucky ball is missing before the robot match!

bolt.d: a robot, captain of the Iron Bolts

tw.r: Red robots race round and round, rrrrunning right to rule the road.
tw.l: Little Lola lifts a lovely ball, and it lands low in the left net.
tw.sz: Six zippy stars zoom and sizzle as the zebra sips Zoe's fizzy juice.
tw.sh: Shy chicks chase shiny shoes and shout, wishing the cheese was cheaper.

x: Match day!
Tomorrow we play the Iron Bolts!
Captain, tomorrow is the big match against the robots, the Iron Bolts! Let's get our star ball!
No ball!
Oh no! The star ball is not on the shelf!
I flew all round: not on the shelf, not under the bench! The ball is gone!
Where is it?
It brings us luck!
Our star ball has brought us luck for three years! We need it. Let's search!
A seed on the floor.
A black seed is lying on the floor.
Captain spots something tiny on the floor: a shiny black seed. Where did it come from?
Locked up!
Zippy's locker is locked. Say the password!
Zippy's locker is locked with a password, and it may hide a clue! Say the password!
What now?
Where shall we look for the ball?
There is one seed but many paths. Do we follow the seeds or ask the neighbours?
More seeds!
There is a trail of seeds! Come on!
Look, a trail of black seeds! It goes all along the path!
It smells of melon!
Nobody saw the ball, but it smells of melon!
The neighbours did not see the ball, but the whole street smells of watermelons. Strange, isn't it?

end: Where is the ball?
Where do the seeds lead?
What are these seeds and where do they lead? We will find out tomorrow!

card.d: Brings luck. But now it is hiding!

x: Seeds in a row!
The seeds lie in a row all the way to the street.
Buzzy zooms along the path: the seeds lie in a neat row, as if someone dropped them on the go.
It's melon!
These are watermelon seeds! Melons went by here!
These are watermelon seeds! So a cart full of watermelons came this way.
I see tracks!
Wheel tracks are left on the ground!
Look: stripes from wheels, and next to them a round dent. It looks like a ball mark!
A cart and a box.
Round the corner stands a cart with a box.
Round the corner stands an empty cart. A box with a lock is tied to it, and the lock says: "Say the password."
Box is shut!
The box on the cart is shut. Say the password!
On the cart is a box with a code lock: it opens if you say the password! Say it.

q: Whose seeds were on the path?

x: What next?
What shall we do next, Captain?
The box holds a note: "We take melons to the market." Do we run to the market now, or call Coach first?
Run to market!
Run to the market before lunch!
Quick, to the market! Melons are sold before lunch, and we must find the ball in time!
I'm with you!
I'm coming! But first a warm-up!
Coach Zippy is already tying his laces. "I'm coming! But first a warm-up, or my legs will sulk!"

end: What's at the market?
What waits for us at the market?
The market is big, with hundreds of melons. How will we find our ball among them?

card.d: It drives slowly but drops seeds fast.

x: Run, team!
Warm-up! Run to the market, march!
A warm-up on the way! In a real match, eleven players play for each team, so we need strength!
I'm quick!
I'm quick! I have six legs!
I'm the smallest, but I have six legs! A goalkeeper must catch fast, and I will!
Pass, pass, pass!
We run and pass to each other!
We pass a sock instead of a ball: pass, pass, pass! A good team plays together.
I see the ball!
I see the star ball among the melons!
Stop! Among the green melons lies a round thing with a star. That is our ball!
Ball in a net!
The melons are under a net. Say the password!
The melons are covered by a net with a magic lock. Say the password to get the ball!
What to say?
How do we get the ball back?
The ball rolled into the cart by mistake and was brought to the market. What shall we do?
It's our ball!
Sorry, this is our star ball!
Sorry, this is our star ball, not a melon! It rolled into the cart by mistake.
Ball and melon!
Coach buys a melon, and we take the ball!
Coach Zippy laughs and buys a melon for the team: the ball is found, time to celebrate!

end: Who is that rumbling?
Who is rumbling by our stadium?
The ball is found! But someone huge is coming to the stadium, rumbling like a hundred pans. Who is it?

card.d: Six legs, and all run after the ball.

x: I am Bolt!
I'm Bolt! We will win! Beep-boop!
I am BOLT, captain of the Iron Bolts. Our chance of winning: a hundred percent. Beep!
Don't worry!
Easy! He is just a show-off!
Easy, Captain! Bolt likes to boast, but he plays fair. Let's answer with a tongue twister!
Word battle!
I challenge you to a tongue twister battle! Beep!
I challenge you to a tongue twister duel. Whoever says it faster and clearer picks half the pitch. Beep-boop!
One, two, three!
I'm the judge! One, two, three, go!
I'm the judge! We take turns, and a slip loses a point. One, two, three, go!
Say it fast!
Battle! Say the twister clearly!
The tongue twister battle has begun! Say it clearly and fast, and Bolt will see who he is playing.
How to answer?
How do we answer Bolt?
Bolt talks very fast, like a robot. Do we answer faster or clearer?
Clear! Beep!
Clearly said! My parts are humming!
Clear and neat! My chips are delighted. But we will still win the match! Beep-boop!
Oh! Beep?
Fast! My gears are stuck!
Fast! My processor got tangled in the sh-sounds. Sh-sh-beep! Fine, that was funny.

end: What will happen?
What will happen at the match?
The battle is over, and dark clouds suddenly gather in the sky. What will the match bring?

card.d: Says "beep" but boasts a whole "beep-boop".

x: Match on!
Whistle! The big match begins!
Whistle! Eleven of ours and eleven robots run onto the pitch, and the ball rolls to the centre.
It's raining!
The first drops fall from the sky!
The first heavy drops fall from the sky, and the grass on the pitch soon gets slippery.
Squeak! Squeak!
Beep! My joints squeak in the water!
Beep-beep! Water got in my joints and they squeak like an old door. It is hard to run.
Match stop!
Stop the game! The robots need help!
Stop the game! The robots need oil, or their joints will rust. Let's help!
Umbrella, open!
We need a huge umbrella! Say the password!
A huge umbrella over the pitch opens only with a password! Say it before the rain gets stronger!

q: How many players does a team have on the pitch?

x: What first?
What do we do first?
What matters more first: cover the pitch with an umbrella or oil the robots?
Umbrella is up!
The umbrella opened! What a size!
A huge umbrella opened over the pitch, and everyone laughs: it is dry even by the farthest goal!
I'll oil them!
Oiling! With quick little legs!
I fly from robot to robot and quickly oil their joints. The squeaks fade! Next!

end: Who will win?
Will the match start again?
The rain fades, the robots shine, and the ball waits in the centre. Who will score first?

card.d: Covers the whole pitch and never leaks.

x: Play! Beep!
Beep-boop! Let's play fair, Captain!
Beep-boop! The Iron Bolts play fair. The match goes by the rules, and goals are won fairly!
I catch it!
I catch the ball! A goalkeeper may use hands!
I catch it! Only the goalkeeper may take the ball in hands, and only in their own penalty box!
We help!
Ball out! Let's help Bolt up!
Bolt slipped and fell. Captain kicks the ball out of play, and everyone runs to help.
Thanks! Beep!
Beep! Thanks for fair play!
Beep-beep! You stopped the game for me. That is fair play. Saving it in my memory!
Say it and shoot!
Power for the kick! Say the password!
The ball lies before the goal: say the password to shoot like a real champion!
How to finish?
How shall we end the match?
The scoreboard shows a tie. Do we play to the end, or invite everyone to play together?
A draw! Beep!
A draw! Three-three! That is fair!
Whistle! Three-three, a draw. Bolt pats a shoulder: "A fair score! Beep-boop!"
All together!
All together! Iron and paws!
Robots and our players mix and play together! The ball flies, and nobody counts goals.

end: We're friends!
Now the robots are our friends!
The star ball is back with the team, and the Iron Bolts are true friends now. What champions!

card.d: One cup for two teams. A draw is cool too!

space.about: A trip to Mars on a rocket that can talk

bip.d: a kind Martian with three eyes

r: Red rocket roar, run, run, run!
l: Little lamp, leap, lead the way!
sz: Zap, buzz, siren, blast off, zoom!
sh: Shhh, the shiny ship is humming!
Shy little chick in a shiny shell!

tw.r: Red Bip in a rusty rucksack rolls the rocket round the rim.
tw.l: Little blue Larry the llama loves licking lemon lollies on the Moon.
tw.sz: Sixty zippy zebras zoom past Saturn, sipping sizzling soda.
tw.sh: A cheeky chick sheds shiny shoes and chats with six chocolate sheep.

x: I'm Spark!
I'm Spark the rocket, and I fly to Mars!
Hello, Captain! I'm Spark, a talking rocket, and we are flying to Mars. Let's say goodbye to Earth!
I'm Comet.
I'm Comet, the crew's engineer. I check it all!
I'm Comet, the crew's engineer. I checked the bolts, I washed my paws, we can fly!
Tanks are full!
Tanks are full, let's start the countdown!
Tanks are full, belts are clipped. Just say the password and the engines will wake up!
Say the password!
The engines wait for a password. Say it!
The engines sleep and wake up only to a password. Say it loudly, Captain!
What to take?
What shall we take on the trip?
There is little room in the rocket. Do we take a favourite book or an experiment kit?
The book comes!
The book comes along. We'll read on the trip!
Comet tucks the book in a pocket: in zero gravity it will float like a fish.
Experiments come!
The experiments come. Good for Mars!
Spark hums: the experiment kit will be useful, there is so much to test on Mars!

end: What is blinking?
Five, four, three... What is blinking?
The countdown has begun: five, four, three... But suddenly a red light blinks on the panel. What is it?

card.d: Talks, worries, and flies anyway!

x: Blast off! Hooray!
The lamp said wave to Earth. Blast off!
The lamp blinked "Wave to Earth"! We wave, and Spark roars up into the sky!
We float!
Comet floats paws up!
Earth drifts past the window, a blue ball with clouds. In zero gravity Comet floats paws up!
There's the Moon!
The Moon! It shows us just one side.
The Moon always faces Earth with the same side, so we never see its far side from Earth.
Hop, hop!
Gravity is weaker here. Hop, hop!
On the Moon gravity is six times weaker than on Earth, and Comet bounces higher than a wardrobe!
Say the password!
Let's switch on the lamp! Password needed.
To make Spark switch on the Moon lamp, we need a password. Say it, Captain!

q: How does the Moon face Earth?
How much weaker is gravity on the Moon?

x: What to do?
What shall we do on the Moon?
Spark awaits orders. What shall we do on the Moon: photograph the craters or have a jump?
Click! A photo!
Click! A photo for the album is ready.
Click! The photo shows craters, marks left by space rocks. There is no wind on the Moon, so nothing wipes them away.
Hop! Hop again!
Hop, hop! We fly like feathers!
Hop, hop! Captain and Comet bounce on the moon dust, and the footprints will stay there for a very long time.

end: What is that cloud?
A red cloud ahead. What is it?
The Moon is left behind, Mars lies ahead, and a huge orange cloud is rising above it. What is it?

card.d: Never wiped away: no wind!

x: A long trip.
Mars is about seven months away.
The trip to Mars lasts about seven months, and Captain and Comet play draughts so they don't get bored.
Mars is red!
There is Mars! It is red from rusty dust.
Mars is red because its dust and rocks are rusty: they hold lots of iron, like an old nail.
Oh, a storm!
Oh! A dust storm is coming!
A dust storm covers the sky with orange haze, and my nozzles tickle. A-a-atchoo!
Password needed!
Close the dust shields? Say the password!
To close the dust shields, we need a password. Say it quickly, Captain!

q: Its dust has lots of iron

x: What to do?
The storm is close. What now?
Spark lands in the orange haze. What will help: switch on the lamps or wait under the shields?
Lights on!
The lamps are on, and we see the way.
Comet switches on the lamps, and two yellow beams flash in the haze. Spark finds a flat spot.
Quiet. We wait.
Shields are shut. We wait quietly.
It is quiet under the shields, like in a little house. Storms on Mars can be long, but this one soon calms down.

end: Who is there?
Someone green taps on the window!
The storm is over, and someone green with three eyes taps on the window. Who is it?

card.d: Orange and noisy, but not scary.

x: Hi! I'm Bip.
Hi! I'm Bip, and I love words!
Hi! I'm Bip. I have three eyes, and my favourite game is words. Shall we play tongue twisters?
A long day!
A day on Mars is a bit longer than ours.
Bip counts: a day on Mars lasts about 24 hours 40 minutes, forty minutes longer than on Earth. Time for a nap!
Two moons!
Mars has two moons: Phobos and Deimos.
The sky of Mars has two tiny moons, Phobos and Deimos. They look like flying potatoes!
Word duel!
Bip invites you to a duel. Ready?
Bip invites you to a tongue twister duel: whoever speaks clearer and faster wins. Ready, Captain?

q: What are the moons of Mars called?
How long is a day on Mars?

x: How to say it?
How shall we say the twister?
Bip waits for an answer. How shall we say it: very fast or slow and clear?
Ha! So fast!
Ha! Fast, but the words stuck together!
Captain rattles so fast that the words stick together, and Bip laughs with all three eyes: a draw, but a funny one!
Wow, so clear!
Wow, so clear! Bip claps.
Captain speaks slowly and clearly, and Bip is delighted: "First clear, then fast. That is how masters learn!"

end: Spark is beeping!
Spark beeps: we have a fuel problem!
Suddenly Spark beeps anxiously: "Captain, look at the fuel gauge!" What is it?

card.d: Three eyes, three rhymes, zero boredom.

x: Low on fuel!
The tanks are nearly empty, and take-off is near!
Landing used a lot of fuel, and the window for going home is short: Earth and Mars line up well about every two years.
A mountain!
That is Olympus, the biggest volcano!
That is Olympus Mons, the biggest volcano in the Solar System, more than twice as tall as Everest!
Look, ice!
Clean ice lies under the dust!
Comet rakes away the orange dust with a paw, and ice glitters below: real frozen water!
That's fuel!
We make fuel for the tanks from ice!
From ice and the carbon dioxide in Mars air we can make fuel. The tanks start to fill!
Say the password!
Start the factory? Password needed!
The fuel factory starts only with a password. Say it, Captain, and the tanks will start to fill!
What to do?
The tanks are full. What now?
The tanks are filling, and time ticks on. What is better: fly at once or check the tanks again?
Let's fly!
The window is open, and we fly home!
The window is open and the tanks are full, so Spark shakes with excitement: home, while the planets line up well!
Tanks are full!
Comet checked it all: the tanks are full.
Comet checks every tank twice and purrs: there is plenty of fuel, with some to spare, and even a little for cream.

end: Will Spark land?
Spark worries: will she land straight?
Soon we fly home, and Spark whispers: "I must land straight on my tail, on my pad. What if I can't?"

card.d: Frozen water and future fuel.

x: Bye, Bip!
Bip waves and gives a red pebble.
Bip gives a red pebble as a keepsake and promises to invent a hundred more tongue twisters for us!
There's Earth!
Months of flying, and now there is Earth!
The trip home takes months again, but with Comet's riddles time flies, and soon a blue ball appears.
Coming down!
I fly into the air. I get warm, but I hold on!
I fly into Earth's air and get a little hot, but that's normal. Now I turn tail down!
Spark stands tall!
Spark stands straight on her pad!
Spark comes down on a pillar of fire and stands straight on her pad, like a true reusable rocket!
Say the password!
The hatch opens with a password. Say it!
To open the hatch and step out on Earth, we need a password. Say it loudly, Captain!

q: How does Spark land on her pad?
Straight, on a pillar of fire

x: What first?
What shall we do first?
Everyone is home! What shall we do first: hug Spark or treat Comet to cream?
Warm Spark!
Spark is warm and hums softly with joy.
Spark's skin is still warm from the trip, and she hums with joy: "I did it! I'm straight on my tail!"
Cream! Meow!
Comet laps the cream and purrs happily.
Comet laps the cream and purrs so loudly that Spark laughs: "The engineer is happy, so everything works!"

end: Hooray! Home!
We are home! A new trip soon!
We are home, and Spark is already refuelling for a new trip: a reusable rocket hates being bored!

card.d: A red keepsake gift from Bip.

detective.about: The cake is gone! Three suspects and one mystery.

shchek.d: a hamster who hides things in his cheeks

r: Right on track: one, two, three!
l: Lamp, lens, let's look at it!
sh: Chh, whose shoes shuffle, shy chap?

tw.r: Three brave crabs rushed round the river, rolling red rocks.
tw.l: Lovely Lily laid lilies along the lake by the little lane.
tw.sz: Sam sizzled six sweet sausages on his sunny, sizzling stove.
tw.sh: Six shy chicks shuffled and chased shiny shells in the shed.

x: Where's my cake?
My party cake is gone from the window!
I baked a huge cake for the whole street and left it to cool on the window, and now the window is empty!
No crumbs!
Look: not one crumb on the window.
Writing it down: the cake was huge, and there is not one crumb on the sill. This is very strange!
Who was near?
Auntie Bramble, who came by your window?
Auntie Bramble, think: who walked near your window today? Hootie will write it all down.
Three neighbours!
Three neighbours walked by the window.
Three walked by the window: Bagel the dog, Fluffy the cat and Cheeks the hamster. Each one was hiding something!
Say the word!
The lens works only with a word!
Hootie's magic lens works only with a special word. Say it, and it will show all the tracks!

q: What is gone from the window?
What is strange on the sill?
What surprised Hootie on the sill?

x: Where to start?
Where shall we start the case?
The case begins! Do we check the clean window first, or talk to a suspicious neighbour?
A red circle!
A red circle is marked on the calendar.
The sill has a clean ring from the plate, and on the wall calendar is a red circle. Is it a special day?
Me? I sniffed daisies!
I just sniffed the daisies by the fence!
I only sniffed the daisies by the fence! Why are you looking at my paws, Detective?

end: Whose tracks?
There are tracks in the flower bed!
Under the window, deep tracks in the wet flower bed! Whose are they? To be continued tomorrow!

card.d: Finds everything, even lost crumbs.

x: Here are tracks!
Deep tracks lie in the wet flower bed.
In the wet flower bed lie deep tracks, each as big as a saucer. Writing it down: they go from the window to the gate.
Deep tracks!
Deep tracks: someone carried something heavy.
A light hamster would leave tiny dots. Deep holes appear when someone carries something heavy, like a huge cake!
Bagel's paws!
Tracks as big as a saucer, like Bagel's paws.
The tracks are saucer-sized. Bagel's paws are like saucers, Fluffy's like coins, and Cheeks's like buttons.
It's not me!
The tracks are mine, but I didn't eat the cake!
Yes, the tracks are mine, I walked by! But I didn't eat the cake. I only love bones!
Lens needs a word!
The lens will show where the tracks go!
The lens can show where the tracks lead, but it needs the magic word. Say it loudly!

q: What does Bagel love to eat?

x: Where to go?
The tracks lead to the gate. Where now?
The tracks stop at the gate. Do we follow the tracks further, or find out who was where in the morning?
Wheels here!
The tracks end, then wheels begin.
At the gate the tracks end, and two wheel lines go on. Someone took the cake away on a cart!
I got cream!
I went for cream all morning, honest!
I went for cream all morning! That's all I know. Well, almost all, purr!

end: Who was where?
Who was where at ten o'clock?
We found tracks, but no cake! Who was where at ten in the morning? To be continued tomorrow!

card.d: As big as a whole saucer!

x: Time matters!
At 10:20 the cake was there, at 10:50 gone.
I flew by at 10:20 and the cake was there. At 10:50 Bramble came back to an empty window. So it vanished in half an hour!
I was at the joiner's!
Till 10:20 at the joiner's, from 10:30 at the fountain.
Till 10:20 I stood at the joiner's, and from 10:30 I splashed my paws in the fountain. Ask the ducks!
At the dairy.
Till 10:30 at the dairy, from 10:40 on the roof.
Till 10:30 I purred at the dairy, and from 10:40 I napped on the roof. The shopkeeper will tell you, meow!
At the seed shop.
Till 10:40 at the seed shop, from 10:50 home.
Till 10:40 I picked seeds, and from 10:50 I sat at home. The seller will tell you: I'm his best customer!
Notebook is shut!
Hootie's notebook opens with a word!
The notebook is locked up. It opens only if you say the special word!
Who took the cake?
Who could take the cake alone?
The cake vanished between 10:20 and 10:50. Let's draw the time on a ruler: who is free and when?
One by one!
Each is free for ten minutes, one after another!
Bagel is free from 10:20 to 10:30, then Fluffy till 10:40, then Cheeks till 10:50. Ten minutes each, in a row!
Quack! At 10:30!
The ducks quack: Bagel came at exactly 10:30!
The ducks quacked together: Bagel came at exactly 10:30, not a minute earlier! But what about 10:20?

end: A relay race?
Was the cake passed along in a relay?
Ten minutes each, one after another! Did they carry the cake away together? To be continued tomorrow!

card.d: All times are noted, even lunch.

x: I out-talk everyone!
Nobody out-talks me, I'm the best chatterbox!
I, Cheeks, can out-talk anyone! I bet nobody can say a twister as fast as I can!
A twister duel!
Shall we have a twister duel, Detective?
Let's have a twister duel: whoever trips loses! Meanwhile I'll see why Cheeks has such round cheeks.
Oops, it's in the way!
Oops, I have something in my mouth!
Oops, something is in my mouth, pfft, no, I'm not in voice today. Another time!
A candle falls out!
A party candle fell out of his cheek!
A little party candle rolled out of Cheeks's cheek! Why does he need it if the cake is gone?
Say the twister!
Cheeks waits, say the twister!
Cheeks is sure he will win. Say the twister without a slip and show who is the word master!

q: What rolled out of Cheeks's cheek?

x: What to do?
A candle! What now?
Cheeks runs off! Do we run after him or look at the candle: maybe it holds a clue?
The candle is new!
The candle is brand new, never lit.
The candle is brand new: not a drop of wax, never lit. Is someone planning a party?
Oops, I'm here again!
I run fast, and I ran back to you!
I run faster than the wind! Oh, where did I run to? Back to you, Detective?

end: Whose party?
A candle, a cake, a circle: what do they mean?
A candle, a missing cake, a red circle on the calendar... What do they mean? To be continued tomorrow!

card.d: Out-talks everyone, until his cheeks are full.

x: No spoon!
My big silver spoon is gone!
And now my big silver spoon is gone too, the one I spread cream on cakes with! Oh dear!
A pink spot!
Fluffy has a pink spot of cream on his paw!
On Fluffy's paw is a pink spot of cream. But his whiskers are clean, so he did not eat the cake!
It's raspberry!
It's raspberry! I only sniffed it, honest!
It's raspberry jam, honest! I was only passing by, and anyway, I must go, purr!
Cream, not jam!
The spot is light: cream, not jam!
Jam is dark, but the spot is light pink: it's Bramble's cream! And pink dots lead along a path to the park.
Switch on the lens!
The lens sees pink dots with a word!
The pink dots are hard to see in the grass. Say the word, and the lens will glow like a torch!

q: What does Bramble spread cream with?

x: Where now?
The dots lead to the park. What to do?
The pink dots lead to the park, to an old summerhouse. Do we sneak up quietly or knock loudly?
Shh! Do you hear?
Whispers and rustling come from the summerhouse.
From the summerhouse come soft whispers, rustling paper and a tiny voice: "Shh, she's coming!"
Closed! We're busy!
Closed! Come back in five minutes!
Closed for cleaning, come back in five minutes, no, ten! Oh, we're not expecting anyone!

end: What's behind the door?
What is hidden in the summerhouse?
Pink dots, a candle, a spoon... Someone whispers behind the summerhouse door! What is it? To be continued tomorrow!

card.d: Silver, big and very useful.

x: No crumbs!
No crumbs, deep tracks, a relay: it all fits!
No crumbs, deep tracks, ten minutes each, a candle and pink cream: it all fits! Nobody ate the cake.
The cake is safe!
The cake is safe! It was carried off for a party!
The cake was not eaten but carried off, I think for a party! The red circle on the calendar is no accident.
What party?
What party? I remember nothing!
What party? I have so much to do that I don't even look at the calendar!
Say the password!
The door opens only with a password!
The door is locked with a magic password. Say it loudly, and the lock will click like in a real detective story!

q: Why was the cake carried off?
What did we find out about the cake?
It was carried off, not eaten

x: How to go in?
The door is open. How do we go in?
The lock clicked! Do we tiptoe in quietly or fling the door open and say "Knock, knock"?
Surprise!
Surprise! Happy birthday, Auntie Bramble!
Surprise! We took the cake away to decorate it for your birthday, Auntie Bramble!
Happy birthday!
We decorated your cake with cream, purr!
I wrote the greeting in cream with Bramble's spoon, and Cheeks hid the candles in his cheeks, ha-ha!

end: Cake for all!
Cake for all! The biggest slice for the Detective!
The cake was cut for the whole street, and nobody missed out. The Detective got the biggest slice, with raspberries!

card.d: Whole, tasty and for the whole street!

dino.about: Professor Shell's clock takes Captain to the dinosaurs

prof.d: a snail, inventor of the clock

hrum.d: a baby Triceratops who crunches leaves

grom.d: a loud T. rex with tiny arms

tw.r: Red Rory the rhino rolled round a rocky ridge, roaring and rejoicing.
tw.l: Lala the llama sang on a hill and licked a lovely lilac lolly.
tw.sz: Six sleepy zebras sipped sizzling soup and snoozed in the sun.
tw.sh: A shy sheep shuffled in the shade, whispering "shh, shh" to six chicks.

x: Here is my clock!
Captain, this is the time clock!
Captain, this is the time clock! It takes you to any age, even a very ancient one.
Crawling to the button!
I have crawled to the button for an hour.
I have been crawling to the button since morning, but I may not get there before evening.
I'll press it!
Professor, let me press it!
Professor, let me press it! Or we will reach the ancient days only by evening.
I'll ride!
I'll ride on your shoulder!
I'll ride on your shoulder, Captain: that way we reach the ancient days faster than by crawling.
Say the password!
The clock asks for a password! Say it!
The clock hums and asks for a password. Say it loudly, Captain, so it can hear you!

q: How long has Shell crawled to the button?
Where can the time clock take you?

x: Someone is crying!
Ferns all around, and someone is crying!
Huge ferns all around, and behind them someone sniffles softly. What do we do?
I'm lost!
I'm Crunchy and I'm lost! Help!
I'm Crunchy! Crunch-crunch is me eating leaves. And I lost my herd. Will you help?
Crunch-crunch! I'm here!
Crunch-crunch! I'm Crunchy, I lost my herd!
Crunch-crunch! It's me, Crunchy! I lost my herd and ate three ferns from sadness.

end: Where's the herd?
Where is Crunchy's herd?
Where do we look for Crunchy's herd? The tracks lead to a huge rock.

card.d: Crawls to the button since morning. But so clever!

x: A track!
Look, someone's huge track is here!
Look, Captain, someone's huge track is here! It is three times bigger than mine.
I'm Rumble! Hi!
RRROAR! It's me, hello, everyone!
RRROAR! It's me, Rumble! I'm just saying hello, my voice is just that loud!
Oh, I'm hiding!
Oh! I'll hide behind you, Captain!
Oh! I'll hide behind you, Captain! That is the biggest T. rex I have ever seen.
Let's be friends!
I wanted to wave, but my arms are short!
I wanted to wave at you, but T. rexes have tiny arms, I can't reach my nose!
Say it loud!
Rumble can't hear! Say the password loud!
Rumble roars so loudly that he can't hear himself. Say the password loud so he knows we are friends!

q: What arms do T. rexes have?

x: What do we do?
Rumble smiles. How do we make friends?
Rumble smiles with his huge mouth. How do we make friends with him, Captain?
They wave at me!
They wave at me! The herd went to the volcano!
They wave at me! I'm so happy that I'll tell you a secret: the herd went to the volcano!
I'll help!
The herd went to the volcano! Let's go!
I'm tall, so I see everything: the herd went to the volcano! Let's go quickly, before it gets dark.

end: What is smoking?
A mountain ahead, and smoke rises!
Ahead stands a tall mountain with smoke rising from it. What waits for Captain there?

card.d: Roars "hello!" so loud that leaves fall.

x: A volcano!
There's the volcano: it smokes and grumbles softly.
There is the volcano! It grumbles and smokes softly, and the ground gently tickles everyone's toes.
Where's the herd?
No herd! Where did it go?
No herd! Only smoke and stones. Not even a leaf left to crunch.
We need help!
We need someone who sees from the sky!
We need someone who sees everything from above! I'm big, but I can't fly, sadly.
Call Feather!
Say the password and call the pterosaur!
Say the password louder, and someone who sees everything will fly down from the sky: the pterosaur, Feather!

q: Who flew down from the sky?

x: Feather flies!
Feather arrived and sees all from above!
Feather arrived! She is not a dinosaur but a flying reptile, and she sees everything around. Where to fly?
I'm flying!
In a flash! I see everything from up here!
In a flash! I see everything from up here, as if on my hand, though I have no hands, only wings.
Follow me!
Follow the trail, I'll fly above you!
Follow the trail, and I'll fly above you and show the way with my wings.

end: What does Rumble want?
Rumble roars: "First, a contest!"
The herd is in sight, but Rumble blocks the way and roars: "First, a contest: who is better at tongue twisters!"

card.d: Flies high, sees all. But she is not a dinosaur!

x: Who is louder?
I'm the loudest! Here are my rules!
I'm the loudest in the forest! Whoever beats me at tongue twisters, I'll show a short way.
You can do it!
You can! I'm cheering for you, Captain!
You can do it, Captain! And I'll crunch leaves loudly to cheer you on!
Listen to me!
I roar, and you repeat after me!
I roar a tongue twister, and you repeat it. Just don't laugh: my roar is ticklish!
The battle begins!
The tongue twister battle begins! Who wins?
The funniest battle in history begins: tongue twisters against loud roaring!
Your turn!
Battle! Say the twister, don't slip!
The battle has begun! Say the twister clearly, and Rumble will try to roar over you: whose tongue is quicker?

q: What does Rumble promise the winner?

x: How to answer?
Rumble waits. How do we answer a roar?
Rumble takes a deep breath and waits. How shall we win: fast or clear?
Fast! Wow!
Wow, so fast! My tongue got tangled!
Wow, so fast! My tongue is tied in a knot, and my little arms can't untie it!
Clear! Loud!
Clear and loud! You're almost like me!
Clear and loud! Not even these mountains have heard such an echo, and they hear everything.

end: The clock dims!
Shell's clock blinks and goes dark!
Rumble lost and roars with laughter! But then Shell's clock blinked, hissed and went dark. What happened?

card.d: Roars so loud the echo asks for quiet.

x: Here's the herd!
Here's the herd! They all have three horns!
Here is my herd! They all have three horns, and I have three little bumps so far: I'm a baby!
All together!
Walking in a herd is safer and more fun!
Plant-eating dinosaurs walked in herds: together is safer and more fun, especially for a baby.
The clock is silent!
The clock is silent! It is out of power!
The clock is silent and its hands don't move! It seems to have run out of power in ancient times.
I have an idea!
The clock can charge with sun or a roar!
An idea! We can wake the clock with the warm sun on a rock or with Rumble's loud roar.
Wake the clock!
Say the password and wake the clock!
The clock is almost asleep. Say the password so it hears you and ticks again!

q: How many horns do grown-ups have?

x: How to charge it?
The clock ticks softly. How to charge it?
The clock ticks very softly. How do we charge it fully: with sun or with a roar?
Tick-tock! Warm!
Tick-tock! The rock is warm, the clock wakes!
Tick-tock! The rock warmed up all day, and the clock wakes up, just like me after breakfast.
I roar! Tick-tock!
RRROAR! The clock ticks like new!
RRROAR! The clock ticks like new! Who would think my roar winds up time?

end: Time to say bye!
Little time! What will Crunchy give?
The clock ticks, but there is power for only one minute. Time to say goodbye! What will Crunchy give as a keepsake?

card.d: Found the herd and crunches with joy again.

x: Here's my track!
Here's my track as a keepsake, Captain!
Here is my track as a keepsake, Captain! I stepped in soft clay, and it came out just right!
Tracks in stone!
Scientists find tracks in stone.
Dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago, and scientists still find their tracks in stone.
Bye, Captain!
Bye, Captain! We won't forget you!
Bye, Captain! We won't forget you, even though you are a guest from the far future.
Birds are kin!
Birds are dinosaurs' descendants, imagine!
Dinosaurs lived long before people, but their descendants, the birds, live right next to us now!
Say the password!
The clock waits to take us home!
The minute is nearly up! Say the password, and the clock will take us home, to our lab.

q: What do scientists find in stone?

x: We're home!
The clock stops: it's the lab!
The clock clicked softly: we are back in Professor Shell's lab! What shall we do with the track?
Track is home!
Crunchy's track now sits on a shelf!
Crunchy's track sits on the shelf: it is like a fossil now, but once it crunched leaves.
To the museum!
We'll take the track to a museum for all to see!
We'll take the track to a museum, and children will see how Triceratops walked millions of years ago!

end: Hooray, we're home!
So the trip through time ended!
So ended the trip to the dinosaurs: Crunchy found his herd, and Captain has a track as a keepsake.

card.d: A small track, a big memory.
